name: sparse_usage_init
prose: Static __init function sparse_usage_init(nid, map_count). It computes size = mem_section_usage_size() * map_count (no overflow check) and sets the global sparse_usagebuf to the result of sparse_early_usemaps_alloc_pgdat_section(NODE_DATA(nid), size). If that is NULL it sets sparse_usagebuf_end to NULL and returns -ENOMEM (sparse_usagebuf is then NULL as well). Otherwise it sets sparse_usagebuf_end = sparse_usagebuf + size and returns 0. The buffer is not freed here, and the later sparse_usage_fini only sets both pointers to NULL without freeing it.
note: Reviewer (round 2) right: sparse_usage_fini just clears the pointers (sparse.c:523-526). Old prose already said this; tightened.

name: overcommit_policy_handler
prose: Static sysctl handler overcommit_policy_handler(table, write, buffer, lenp, ppos). On read (write == 0) it returns proc_dointvec_minmax(table, ...) and does not change sysctl_overcommit_memory. On write it copies the table entry, points the copy's data at a local new_policy initialized to -1 and calls proc_dointvec_minmax on the copy. If that returns non-zero, or leaves new_policy at -1 (nothing was parsed), it returns the call's result (0 in the second case) without changing sysctl_overcommit_memory. Otherwise it calls mm_compute_batch(new_policy) for whatever value was accepted, calls schedule_on_each_cpu(sync_overcommit_as) only when new_policy is OVERCOMMIT_NEVER, stores new_policy into sysctl_overcommit_memory, and returns 0. It takes no lock itself.
note: Reviewer right that the batch is recomputed for every accepted policy, not only OVERCOMMIT_NEVER (util.c:802-805); the old prose here already described that correctly.

name: vm_commit_limit
prose: Returns the committed-memory limit used with OVERCOMMIT_NEVER as an unsigned long. If sysctl_overcommit_kbytes is non-zero the base is sysctl_overcommit_kbytes >> (PAGE_SHIFT - 10); otherwise it is (totalram_pages() - hugetlb_total_pages()) * sysctl_overcommit_ratio / 100. In both cases total_swap_pages is added before returning. The arithmetic is unsigned long and is not checked for overflow. It reads global sysctls and counters and takes no lock.
note: Old prose matches util.c:875-887; no reviewer claim left (old contract was dropped).

name: vm_memory_committed
prose: Returns percpu_counter_sum_positive(&vm_committed_as): the counter's central value plus every CPU's local count (summed under the counter's own spinlock), clamped to 0 if the sum is negative, as an unsigned long. It takes no other lock or reference.
note: Matches util.c:908-911.

name: __split_vma
prose: Static __must_check function __split_vma(vmi, vma, addr, new_below) splitting vma at addr; the caller is expected to hold the mmap write lock and addr must lie strictly inside vma (violations only trigger WARN_ON). If vma->vm_ops->may_split exists and returns non-zero that error is returned first. Otherwise it duplicates the VMA (-ENOMEM if vm_area_dup fails), sets the new VMA to cover [vm_start, addr) when new_below is non-zero or [addr, vm_end) otherwise (adjusting vm_pgoff), and preallocates the maple-tree store (-ENOMEM if vma_iter_prealloc fails). It then duplicates the memory policy (failure: returns that error after freeing the iterator state and the new VMA, without calling mpol_put) and calls anon_vma_clone (failure: returns that error after mpol_put on the new VMA's policy, freeing the iterator state and the new VMA). On success it takes a file reference on new->vm_file if present, calls new->vm_ops->open if present, write-locks both VMAs (vma_start_write), adjusts transparent-huge-page and hugetlb state at the boundary, shrinks vma (moving its start up and advancing vm_pgoff when new_below, or moving its end down otherwise), calls vma_complete, which stores the new VMA in the maple tree, and returns 0. The iterator is then advanced (vma_next when new_below, vma_prev otherwise) so that it points at the original vma.
note: Reviewer 15 right: mpol_put only on the anon_vma_clone failure path (vma.c:530-532, 574-575); vma_dup_policy failure jumps to out_free_vmi (526-528). Reviewer 2 right: iterator ends on the original vma after vma_next/vma_prev (566-570). Old prose also overstated 'maple tree unchanged' (not stated in code; only the preallocation is freed).

name: vma_merge_existing_range
prose: Static __must_check function vma_merge_existing_range(vmg) that tries to merge a modified range of vmg->middle with its neighbours. The caller must hold the mmap write lock and vmg->middle must be set; vmg->next must be unset, the range must satisfy the WARN conditions on prev/start/end, and vmg->copied_from must be NULL (these are only checked with WARNs). It sets vmg->state = VMA_MERGE_NOMERGE, and returns NULL right away if vmg->vm_flags has VM_SPECIAL or the range touches neither the start nor the end of middle. If the range starts at middle's start it checks can_vma_merge_left; if it ends at middle's end it looks up next (storing it in vmg->next, which stays set on all later returns) and checks can_vma_merge_right. If neither merge applies it returns NULL with state NOMERGE. If merge_left, the iterator is moved back to prev. If the range spans the whole of middle (so middle would be deleted) and can_merge_remove_vma(middle) is false it returns NULL. If both neighbours would merge but next cannot be removed, it clears __remove_next, merge_right and merge_both and carries on with only the left merge. It then calls vma_start_write on middle and on the merge neighbours, sets vmg->target (prev for a left merge, else next) and extends the sticky flags, adjusts vmg->start, end and pgoff and the __adjust_*/__remove_* fields for the merge shape, and calls dup_anon_vma as needed. If dup_anon_vma or commit_merge fails, it positions the iterator back at the original start and loads it, unlinks any duplicated anon_vma, sets vmg->state to VMA_MERGE_ERROR_NOMEM unless vmg->give_up_on_oom is set (then it stays NOMERGE) and returns NULL; the vmg fields changed above are not restored, and the VMAs already write-locked stay locked. On success it sets the sticky flags on vmg->target, calls khugepaged_enter_vma, sets state VMA_MERGE_SUCCESS and returns vmg->target.
note: Reviewer 1 right that the early-abort paths do not restore the iterator (vma.c:844-876; only the abort label at 981-983 does). Reviewer 2 right that non-removable next is not an abort (888-892). Old prose also said vma_start_write is done only on success; in fact it happens before commit_merge (895-907) and stays after an abort.

name: zswap_compressor_param_set
prose: Static module-parameter setter zswap_compressor_param_set(val, kp) for the zswap compressor; kp->arg points to the current compressor string. It strips whitespace from val, and under zswap_init_lock switches on zswap_init_state: ZSWAP_UNINIT calls param_set_charp and returns its result (0 or its error) without creating any pool; ZSWAP_INIT_FAILED returns -ENODEV; ZSWAP_INIT_SUCCEED returns 0 without changes if a pool exists and the name equals the current compressor, otherwise it goes on to create or switch pools. For the switch, it returns -ENOENT (after an error message) if crypto_has_acomp rejects the name. Under zswap_pools_lock it looks for an existing pool of that name (zswap_pool_find_get) and, if found, removes it from the list and later resurrects its reference; otherwise it calls zswap_pool_create, and if that returns NULL the result is -EINVAL. When a pool exists it calls param_set_charp to store the name. If the result is 0, the previously current pool is remembered, the new pool is added at the head of zswap_pools and zswap_has_pool is set; if storing failed but a pool exists (pre-existing or newly created), that pool is appended to the tail of zswap_pools. After the lock is dropped, percpu_ref_kill is called on the remembered pool (the old current pool on success, the unused pool on a failed store). It returns 0 on success or the error described. The function takes zswap_init_lock and zswap_pools_lock internally and may sleep.
note: Reviewer 15 is wrong for the INIT_SUCCEED path: param_set_charp is called after the pool was found or created (zswap.c:~552-555), and on failure the pool is appended to the tail and killed (562-571); it is right only for ZSWAP_UNINIT where param_set_charp is called early with no pool involved (494-497). Old prose merged the two cases. -EINVAL on pool create failure was already in the old prose; added the -ENOENT and existing-pool details.

name: br2684_init
prose: Static __init function br2684_init(). With CONFIG_PROC_FS enabled it calls proc_create_seq("br2684", 0, atm_proc_root, &br2684_seq_ops) and returns -ENOMEM if that returns NULL, before registering anything. Otherwise (and always when CONFIG_PROC_FS is off, in which case no proc entry is created) it calls register_atm_ioctl(&br2684_ioctl_ops) and register_atmdevice_notifier(&atm_dev_notifier), ignoring their return values, and returns 0.
note: Reviewer (round 1) right: without CONFIG_PROC_FS no proc entry is created (br2684.c:828-833); the old prose handled it but is tightened. Return values of the register calls are ignored in the code.

name: atm_proc_exit
prose: Static inline stub of atm_proc_exit(void) in net/atm/common.h for builds without CONFIG_PROC_FS: an empty function that does nothing and returns nothing. When CONFIG_PROC_FS is enabled the header only declares atm_proc_exit (the real function is defined elsewhere, in the ATM proc code), so this description covers the stub only.
note: Reviewer (round 1) right that the old text described only the stub; scope now stated. Kept rather than dropped because the stub is a function (common.h:39-45 #else branch).

name: ax25_connect
prose: Static __must_check function ax25_connect(sock, uaddr, addr_len, flags) for an AX.25 socket. Before taking any lock it returns -EINVAL if addr_len is not sizeof(struct sockaddr_ax25), not sizeof(struct full_sockaddr_ax25) and not in the range [sizeof(struct sockaddr_ax25) + 6*sizeof(ax25_address), sizeof(struct full_sockaddr_ax25)], or if sax25_family is not AF_AX25. It then takes lock_sock and releases it on every later return. Restart handling (sock->state == SS_CONNECTING): sk_state TCP_SYN_SENT returns -EINPROGRESS; TCP_ESTABLISHED sets SS_CONNECTED and returns 0; TCP_CLOSE sets SS_UNCONNECTED and returns -ECONNREFUSED; other sk_state values fall through to a new attempt. An established SOCK_SEQPACKET socket returns -EISCONN. Otherwise it sets sk_state to TCP_CLOSE and sock->state to SS_UNCONNECTED, and frees and clears the old ax25->digipeat. If a digipeater list is supplied it returns -EINVAL for a count outside 1..AX25_MAX_DIGIS or an addr_len too short for it, -ENOBUFS if allocation fails, otherwise builds the digipeater list. It then returns -EINVAL if the socket is still SOCK_ZAPPED (unbound) and -EHOSTUNREACH if no device is attached (the new list is freed in these two cases); for SOCK_SEQPACKET it returns -EADDRINUSE if ax25_find_cb finds an identical connection (list freed, found control block released with ax25_cb_put). The state reset above is not undone on these error returns. On success paths the destination address and the digipeater list are stored in ax25. A non-SEQPACKET socket becomes SS_CONNECTED/TCP_ESTABLISHED and returns 0. A SEQPACKET socket becomes SS_CONNECTING/TCP_SYN_SENT, starts establishing the data link and the heartbeat, and returns -EINPROGRESS if O_NONBLOCK is set and not yet established; otherwise it sleeps (dropping the lock while scheduling) until sk_state changes, returning -ERESTARTSYS if a signal arrives (state left SS_CONNECTING). If it ends not established it sets SS_UNCONNECTED and returns sock_error(sk); if established it sets SS_CONNECTED and returns 0.
note: Reviewer 15 is wrong about -ECONNREFUSED: it is returned on the restart path when sk_state is TCP_CLOSE (af_ax25.c:1273-1276), separately from the sock_error() return at 1417. Old prose said the lock is taken before the digipeater list is freed 'otherwise'; the code first handles restarts and -EISCONN. Slice cut the head (function at 1230).

name: ax25_ioctl
prose: Static function ax25_ioctl(sock, cmd, arg), the ioctl handler for AX.25 sockets. It takes lock_sock(sk), handles the command, releases the lock and returns the result. TIOCOUTQ and TIOCINQ write the amount (send-buffer room or the length of the first queued receive skb) with put_user, giving 0 or -EFAULT. SIOCAX25ADDUID, SIOCAX25DELUID and SIOCAX25GETUID copy a sockaddr_ax25 from user space (-EFAULT on failure) and return ax25_uid_ioctl's result. SIOCAX25NOUID returns -EPERM without CAP_NET_ADMIN, -EFAULT if get_user fails, -EINVAL if the value is below 0 or above AX25_NOUID_BLOCK, otherwise sets ax25_uid_policy and returns 0. SIOCADDRT, SIOCDELRT and SIOCAX25OPTRT require CAP_NET_ADMIN (else -EPERM) and return ax25_rt_ioctl's result; SIOCAX25CTLCON likewise with ax25_ctl_ioctl. SIOCAX25ADDFWD and SIOCAX25DELFWD require CAP_NET_ADMIN (else -EPERM), copy a struct from user space (-EFAULT on failure) and return ax25_fwd_ioctl's result. SIOCAX25GETINFO and SIOCAX25GETINFOOLD copy the control block's statistics to user space: for the old command a one-time message is logged and a copy_to_user failure returns -EFAULT; for the new command a copy_to_user failure returns -EINVAL; otherwise both return 0. The address and metric ioctls SIOCGIFADDR, SIOCSIFADDR, SIOCGIFDSTADDR, SIOCSIFDSTADDR, SIOCGIFBRDADDR, SIOCSIFBRDADDR, SIOCGIFNETMASK, SIOCSIFNETMASK, SIOCGIFMETRIC and SIOCSIFMETRIC unconditionally return -EINVAL. Any other cmd returns -ENOIOCTLCMD.
note: All three reviewer claims right: GETINFO copy_to_user failure is -EINVAL (af_ax25.c:1937-1939), GETINFOOLD is -EFAULT (1932-1934), and the SIOC[GS]IF* commands return -EINVAL with no copy (1961-1972). The old sentence blurred them.

name: ax25_ds_state2_machine
prose: Static function ax25_ds_state2_machine(ax25, skb, frametype, pf, type), the DAMA-slave state 2 handler; skb and type are not used. It switches on frametype and always falls to a single return of 0. AX25_SABM or AX25_SABME: sends a DISC command with AX25_POLLON and calls ax25_dama_off. AX25_DISC: sends a UA response with the received pf, calls ax25_dama_off and then ax25_disconnect(ax25, 0). AX25_DM or AX25_UA: if pf is non-zero it calls ax25_dama_off and ax25_disconnect(ax25, 0) and sends nothing; with pf zero it does nothing. AX25_I, AX25_REJ, AX25_RNR or AX25_RR: if pf is non-zero it sends a DISC command with AX25_POLLON and calls ax25_dama_off, without calling ax25_disconnect; with pf zero it does nothing. Any other frame type does nothing.
note: Both reviewer claims are already reflected in the packet prose and are correct against the code (ax25_ds_in.c:117-133: DM/UA with pf disconnect without DISC; I/REJ/RNR/RR with pf send DISC without disconnect). Kept; wording tightened.

name: ax25_std_heartbeat_expiry
prose: Function ax25_std_heartbeat_expiry(ax25), the heartbeat timer expiry handler for the standard (non-DAMA) AX.25 state machine. If ax25->sk is non-NULL it takes bh_lock_sock on it. In state AX25_STATE_0 or AX25_STATE_2: if sk is NULL, or SOCK_DESTROY is set, or the socket is in TCP_LISTEN with SOCK_DEAD set, it destroys the control block with ax25_destroy_socket (for a non-NULL sk it holds a socket reference around that call, unlocks the socket and then drops the reference) and returns without restarting the heartbeat. In states 3 and 4, if sk is non-NULL, sk_rmem_alloc is below half of sk_rcvbuf and AX25_COND_OWN_RX_BUSY is set, it clears AX25_COND_OWN_RX_BUSY and AX25_COND_ACK_PENDING and sends an RR response with AX25_POLLOFF. In every other case (including after sending that RR, and in other states) it unlocks the socket if it was locked and calls ax25_start_heartbeat(ax25).
note: Both reviewer claims already match the code: sk NULL in state 0/2 destroys the block (ax25_std_timer.c:41-52) and the heartbeat is restarted after the RR response (68, 73-76). Kept; tightened.

name: ax25_std_t1timer_expiry
prose: Function ax25_std_t1timer_expiry(ax25), the T1 timer expiry handler of the standard AX.25 state machine. ax25->sk is dereferenced in state AX25_STATE_2 without a NULL check, and the state-1 extended-modulus path reads ax25->ax25_dev. State 1, n2count == n2: with modulus AX25_MODULUS it calls ax25_disconnect(ax25, ETIMEDOUT) and returns without restarting T1; otherwise it sets modulus to AX25_MODULUS, reloads the window from the device values, sets n2count to 0 and sends SABM with AX25_POLLON, then continues to the T1 restart. State 1, n2count != n2: increments n2count and sends SABM (normal modulus) or SABME (extended), then continues. State 2, n2count == n2: sends DISC with AX25_POLLON, calls ax25_disconnect(ax25, ETIMEDOUT) unless SOCK_DESTROY is set on ax25->sk, and returns without restarting T1; n2count != n2: increments it, sends DISC and continues. State 3: n2count = 1, ax25_std_transmit_enquiry, state becomes AX25_STATE_4, continue. State 4, n2count == n2: sends a DM response, calls ax25_disconnect(ax25, ETIMEDOUT) and returns without restarting T1; otherwise increments n2count, transmits an enquiry and continues. Other states just continue. Continuing means ax25_calculate_t1 and ax25_start_t1timer are called.
note: Reviewer claims already match the code and the packet prose (SOCK_DESTROY skip at ax25_std_timer.c:146-147; extended-modulus path zeroes n2count at 131). Kept; tightened.

name: batadv_frag_send_packet
prose: Function batadv_frag_send_packet(skb, orig_node, neigh_node) in net/batman-adv/fragmentation.c (the slice contained only part of it, and its name was not given), which splits skb into up to BATADV_FRAG_MAX_FRAGMENTS fragments and sends them through neigh_node. It uses the incoming interface's MTU limited by BATADV_FRAG_MAX_FRAG_SIZE to compute the fragment size. It always consumes skb: on every path either the skb (or its remaining part) is sent or freed with kfree_skb, and the primary-interface reference, once taken, is released. Failures: -EINVAL if skb->len is 0 or the fragment size is 0, or if no primary interface is selected; -EAGAIN if more than BATADV_FRAG_MAX_FRAGMENTS fragments would be needed; -ENOMEM if skb has a frag_list and __skb_linearize fails, or if batadv_frag_create returns NULL; -EINVAL if the fragment number would reach BATADV_FRAG_MAX_FRAGMENTS - 1 inside the loop; NET_XMIT_DROP if sending a non-final fragment returns anything other than NET_XMIT_SUCCESS (the remaining skb is freed); the negative error of skb_cow_head if there is not enough head room for the last fragment. Otherwise it sends the remaining skb as the last fragment with the fragment header and returns the result of batadv_send_unicast_skb for it unchanged (it may be NET_XMIT_SUCCESS or another transmit status such as NET_XMIT_CN), not normalized.
note: Name was an invented placeholder; the function is batadv_frag_send_packet (fragmentation.c:487-624). Reviewer right that the last send's result is returned raw (621); only non-final fragment failures are mapped to NET_XMIT_DROP (610-613). Old prose also said -EAGAIN/-EINVAL correctly but implied NET_XMIT_SUCCESS only.

name: batadv_mcast_init
prose: Static inline stub of batadv_mcast_init(bat_priv) in net/batman-adv/multicast.h for builds without CONFIG_BATMAN_ADV_MCAST: it does not touch bat_priv, has no side effects and returns 0 as an int. When CONFIG_BATMAN_ADV_MCAST is enabled the header instead declares a void batadv_mcast_init implemented elsewhere, so this description covers the stub only.
note: Reviewer (round 15) right that the CONFIG_BATMAN_ADV_MCAST declaration is void (multicast.h:51) and 'returns 0, no effect' is only the stub at 91-94; scope stated.

name: batadv_hardif_neigh_dump
prose: Function batadv_hardif_neigh_dump(msg, cb) in net/batman-adv/originator.c (the packet slice held only its tail and the placeholder name does not exist), a netlink dump handler for neighbour information. It looks up the mesh interface with batadv_netlink_get_meshif and returns its error (PTR_ERR) if that fails. It then takes the selected primary interface; if there is none, or its if_status is not BATADV_IF_ACTIVE, it returns -ENOENT. It then looks up the hard interface with batadv_netlink_get_hardif: an error other than -ENONET is returned; -ENONET means no hard interface was named and BATADV_IF_DEFAULT (NULL) is used instead. If the routing algorithm has no neigh.dump handler it returns -EOPNOTSUPP. Otherwise it calls bat_priv->algo_ops->neigh.dump(msg, cb, bat_priv, hard_iface) and returns msg->len. All returns after the lookups release what was taken: batadv_hardif_put on the hard interface (a no-op for NULL), batadv_hardif_put on the primary interface, and dev_put on the mesh interface, each once.
note: Name was a placeholder; function is batadv_hardif_neigh_dump (originator.c:752-805). Old prose matches the code; added that BATADV_IF_DEFAULT is NULL (main.h:84, batadv_hardif_put returns on NULL).

name: batadv_tp_meter_recv
prose: Function batadv_tp_meter_recv(bat_priv, skb), void. If bat_priv->mesh_state is not BATADV_MESH_ACTIVE it skips the dispatch. Otherwise it reads the subtype from skb->data (a batadv_icmp_tp_packet) and calls batadv_tp_recv_msg for BATADV_TP_MSG, batadv_tp_recv_ack for BATADV_TP_ACK, and for any other subtype only logs a debug message. On every path it then calls consume_skb(skb) once, so the skb is freed by this function.
note: Reviewer's point (unknown subtype only logs) is already in the packet prose and matches tp_meter.c:1570-1574. Kept; tightened.

name: hci_connect_bis
prose: Function hci_connect_bis(hdev, dst, dst_type, sid, qos, base_len, base, timeout). It calls hci_bind_bis and returns its error pointer unchanged if it fails. If the returned connection is already BT_CONNECTED it returns it immediately (no SID allocation, no marking, nothing queued). Otherwise, if conn->sid is HCI_SID_INVALID it assigns the first SID in 0..0x0f for which hci_find_adv_sid finds no use (if none is free conn->sid stays invalid). It then calls hci_conn_hash_list_state over BT_BOUND BIS_LINK connections with bis_mark_per_adv, which sets HCI_CONN_PER_ADV on each such connection whose dst is BDADDR_ANY, whose big matches qos->bcast.big, and whose bis equals qos->bcast.bis with that bis not BT_ISO_QOS_BIS_UNSET. It then queues create_big_sync with hci_cmd_sync_queue, passing hci_conn_get(conn) as the argument and create_big_complete as the completion. On success it returns conn. If queueing fails, it calls hci_conn_drop(conn) and hci_conn_put(conn) (the put releases the reference taken by hci_conn_get, the drop releases a hold on the connection) and returns ERR_PTR(err); the connection pointer is not returned in that case.
note: Reviewer 15 right: the error path performs both hci_conn_drop and hci_conn_put (hci_conn.c:2360-2363), so it releases more than the extra get; the old claim that the caller still owns the hci_bind_bis reference was not supported. Reviewer 1 right (connected early return at 2330-2331). Reviewer 2 right (dst BDADDR_ANY gate in bis_mark_per_adv, 2306-2308). Old prose also wrongly implied hci_connect_bis had a different parameter list (dst_type, sid, base_len, base, timeout omitted).

name: hci_inquiry_complete_evt
prose: Static function hci_inquiry_complete_evt(hdev, data, skb), handler for the HCI inquiry-complete event; data is a struct hci_ev_status, whose status is only read for the debug message. If the HCI_INQUIRY flag is not set (test_and_clear_bit), it returns with no further effect. Otherwise the flag is cleared, smp_mb__after_atomic is executed, wake_up_bit is called, and if HCI_MGMT is not set it returns. With HCI_MGMT set it takes the hdev lock; if the discovery state is not DISCOVERY_FINDING it just unlocks and returns. If it is DISCOVERY_FINDING: when the resolve list is empty, the state becomes DISCOVERY_STOPPED unless HCI_LE_SCAN is set and HCI_QUIRK_SIMULTANEOUS_DISCOVERY applies (then the state is unchanged). If the resolve list is not empty, it looks up a NAME_NEEDED entry; if one exists and hci_resolve_name returns 0, the entry's name_state becomes NAME_PENDING, the discovery state becomes DISCOVERY_RESOLVING and name_resolve_timeout is set to jiffies + NAME_RESOLVE_DURATION; otherwise the same STOPPED rule as for the empty list applies. The hdev lock is released on every path on which it was taken.
note: Reviewer 15 right: ev->status is read in bt_dev_dbg (hci_event.c:2972), so 'does not inspect' was too strong. Reviewers 1 and 2 right and already reflected in the packet prose (early returns at 2974-2981, lock taken before the FINDING test at 2983-2986).

name: hci_link_key_request_evt
prose: Static function hci_link_key_request_evt(hdev, data, skb), handler for the HCI link-key-request event. If HCI_MGMT is not set it returns immediately without taking the device lock or sending a command. Otherwise it takes the hdev lock and looks up a stored link key for ev->bdaddr; if there is none it sends HCI_OP_LINK_KEY_NEG_REPLY for that address. If a key is found it looks up an ACL connection for the address. When a connection exists, it clears HCI_CONN_NEW_LINK_KEY on it, and then rejects the key (sending the negative reply) if the key type is HCI_LK_UNAUTH_COMBINATION_P192 or _P256 and conn->auth_type is not 0xff and has bit 0 set, or if the key type is HCI_LK_COMBINATION with pin_len below 16 and the connection's pending_sec_level is BT_SECURITY_HIGH or BT_SECURITY_FIPS; if it is not rejected it applies conn_set_key(conn, key->type, key->pin_len). With no matching connection, or after passing those checks, it sends HCI_OP_LINK_KEY_REPLY with the address and the stored key value. The hdev lock is released before returning in all paths after it was taken, and exactly one command is sent after the HCI_MGMT check.
note: Reviewer 15 right: the connection lookup and the clear_bit of HCI_CONN_NEW_LINK_KEY happen only after a key was found (hci_event.c:4627-4637); the old wording implied it whenever a connection matched. Slice cut the head (function begins at 4612).

name: hci_dev_setup_sync
prose: Static function hci_dev_setup_sync(hdev). It returns 0 immediately if neither HCI_SETUP is set nor HCI_QUIRK_NON_PERSISTENT_SETUP is set. Otherwise it emits HCI_DEV_SETUP through hci_sock_dev_event and, if hdev->setup exists, calls it and keeps its return value in ret. It then logs a warning for each quirk from hci_broken_table that is set, and records invalid_bdaddr = HCI_QUIRK_INVALID_BDADDR or HCI_QUIRK_USE_BDADDR_PROPERTY. Only if ret is 0 (setup succeeded or absent): when HCI_QUIRK_USE_BDADDR_PROPERTY is set and public_addr is BDADDR_ANY it tries to read the address from the property, and when invalid_bdaddr is true, public_addr is not BDADDR_ANY and hdev->set_bdaddr exists it calls set_bdaddr, clearing invalid_bdaddr only if that call returns 0 (a failure leaves ret non-zero and invalid_bdaddr true). It then sets HCI_UNCONFIGURED if HCI_QUIRK_EXTERNAL_CONFIG is set or invalid_bdaddr is still true. If HCI_UNCONFIGURED is set (also when it was already set before) it returns hci_unconf_init_sync(hdev), so an earlier error in ret is discarded; otherwise it returns ret (0, or the error from hdev->setup, or from set_bdaddr only if that left HCI_UNCONFIGURED clear, which cannot occur because a failure keeps invalid_bdaddr true). It takes no lock itself.
note: Reviewer 15 right: the BDADDR property lookup and set_bdaddr run only when ret == 0 (hci_sync.c:5133-5144), which the old prose did not say. Reviewer 1 right that when set_bdaddr succeeds invalid_bdaddr is cleared and UNCONFIGURED may stay clear; the old prose already covered it.

name: hci_suspend_sync
prose: Function hci_suspend_sync(hdev). If hdev->suspended is already true it returns 0 with no change. Otherwise it sets hdev->suspended = true and calls hci_pause_discovery_sync, hci_pause_advertising_sync, hci_suspend_monitor_sync and hci_pause_scan_sync. If hci_conn_count(hdev) is non-zero it calls hci_disconnect_all_sync(hdev, HCI_ERROR_REMOTE_POWER_OFF); if that returns an error it sets hdev->suspend_state = BT_RUNNING, calls hci_resume_sync(hdev) and returns the error; on success it calls hci_set_event_mask_sync. Then, if hdev->wakeup is NULL or hdev->wakeup(hdev) returns false, it sets suspend_state = BT_SUSPEND_DISCONNECT and returns 0. Otherwise it sets scanning_paused = false, calls hci_update_event_filter_sync and hci_update_passive_scan_sync, sets scanning_paused = true again, sets suspend_state = BT_SUSPEND_CONFIGURE_WAKE and returns 0.
note: Prose checked against hci_sync.c:6375-6437; removed the unverified parenthetical about what hci_resume_sync does. Slice cut the head (function starts at 6375). No reviewer claim.

name: hci_le_ext_directed_advertising_sync
prose: Static function hci_le_ext_directed_advertising_sync(hdev, conn), which sets up extended directed advertising on instance 0. It calls hci_update_random_address_sync and hci_get_random_address (both with require_privacy false and the RPA choice from conn_use_rpa(conn)), returning the first error. It then builds the extended advertising parameters (legacy direct-ind event type, instance handle 0, the connection's destination address and type), removes advertising instance 0 with hci_remove_ext_adv_instance_sync, sets the parameters with hci_set_ext_adv_params_sync, sets the advertising data with hci_set_ext_adv_data_sync, and, if own_addr_type is ADDR_LE_DEV_RANDOM and the obtained random address is neither BDADDR_ANY nor equal to hdev->random_addr, sets the advertising-set random address with hci_set_adv_set_random_addr_sync. Each of these steps returns its error code immediately on failure. Finally it returns the result of hci_enable_ext_advertising_sync(hdev, 0), so a failure of the enable step is returned after that command was issued; earlier failures mean the enable was never attempted.
note: Packet prose already has the order remove-then-set-params and the enable-failure case correct (hci_sync.c:6573-6596), so both reviewer claims concern an older wording. Added the first two calls' exact names.

name: iso_sock_connect
prose: Static function iso_sock_connect(sock, addr, alen, flags) for a Bluetooth ISO socket. Without taking the lock it returns -EINVAL if alen is less than sizeof(struct sockaddr_iso) or addr->sa_family is not AF_BLUETOOTH. It then takes lock_sock and returns -EBADFD if sk_state is neither BT_OPEN nor BT_BOUND or if BT_SK_CONNECTING is already set (in that case the bit is left as another caller set it); returns -EINVAL if sk_type is not SOCK_SEQPACKET or the address type is not an LE type. These error paths release the lock and do not set BT_SK_CONNECTING. Otherwise it sets BT_SK_CONNECTING, stores the destination address and type in iso_pi(sk), releases the lock, and calls iso_connect_cis if the destination is not BDADDR_ANY, else iso_connect_bis. It retakes the lock and clears BT_SK_CONNECTING. If the connect call failed, that error is returned; if BT_SK_DEFER_SETUP is set it returns 0; otherwise it returns the result of bt_sock_wait_state(sk, BT_CONNECTED, sock_sndtimeo(sk, flags & O_NONBLOCK)), which is 0 or a negative error such as a timeout or interruption. The socket lock is released on every return after it was taken.
note: Both reviewers right: BT_SK_CONNECTING is not cleared on the -EBADFD path when it was already set (iso.c:1171-1175); the old sentence claimed it was clear on all early paths.

name: l2cap_tx_state_wait_f
prose: Static function l2cap_tx_state_wait_f(chan, control, skbs, event), the L2CAP ERTM transmit state machine handler for the WAIT_F state; it returns nothing. control must be non-NULL for L2CAP_EV_RECV_REQSEQ_AND_FBIT (it is dereferenced) and skbs non-NULL for L2CAP_EV_DATA_REQUEST. By event: L2CAP_EV_DATA_REQUEST: sets tx_send_head to skb_peek(skbs) if it was NULL and splices skbs onto the tail of tx_q without sending. L2CAP_EV_LOCAL_BUSY_DETECTED: sets CONN_LOCAL_BUSY, calls l2cap_abort_rx_srej_sent if rx_state is L2CAP_RX_STATE_SREJ_SENT, and calls l2cap_send_ack. L2CAP_EV_LOCAL_BUSY_CLEAR: clears CONN_LOCAL_BUSY; only if CONN_RNR_SENT is set it sends an RR S-frame with the poll bit and reqseq = buffer_seq, sets retry_count to 1, sets the monitor timer and sets tx_state to L2CAP_TX_STATE_WAIT_F. L2CAP_EV_RECV_REQSEQ_AND_FBIT: calls l2cap_process_reqseq(chan, control->reqseq) and then does the same as L2CAP_EV_RECV_FBIT: if control is non-NULL and control->final is set, it clears the monitor timer, sets the retransmission timer if unacked_frames > 0, sets retry_count to 0 and tx_state to L2CAP_TX_STATE_XMIT. L2CAP_EV_EXPLICIT_POLL and any other event do nothing. L2CAP_EV_MONITOR_TO: if max_tx is 0 or retry_count < max_tx it sends an RR or RNR with the poll bit, restarts the monitor timer and increments retry_count (max_tx == 0 means no limit); otherwise it calls l2cap_send_disconn_req(chan, ECONNABORTED).
note: Prose matches l2cap_core.c:2889-2964. Both reviewers' points (max_tx == 0 retries without limit; control/skbs dereferenced for certain events) are already reflected in the packet text and correct.

name: l2cap_select_mode
prose: Static inline function l2cap_select_mode(mode, remote_feat_mask). If mode is L2CAP_MODE_STREAMING or L2CAP_MODE_ERTM and l2cap_mode_supported(mode, remote_feat_mask) returns non-zero, it returns mode. In every other case (any other mode value including L2CAP_MODE_BASIC, or a mode that l2cap_mode_supported rejects) it returns L2CAP_MODE_BASIC. l2cap_mode_supported also depends on the global local feature mask l2cap_feat_mask and the disable_ertm setting, not only on the remote mask. It has no other effect.
note: Reviewer 15 right: the result also depends on local support via l2cap_mode_supported (l2cap_core.c:1522-1536), so the old formal contract (remote mask only) was wrong and is removed; reviewer 1 right that mode==0 returns BASIC (0). No contract because the function reads global state.

name: l2cap_ecred_conn_req
prose: Static inline function l2cap_ecred_conn_req(conn, cmd, cmd_len, data) handling an incoming L2CAP enhanced credit-based connection request. It returns -EINVAL without doing anything if the module option enable_ecred is false; otherwise it returns 0 on every path. It builds an L2CAP_ECRED_CONN_RSP (rsp_len is the SCID list length of the request, or 0 for rejections decided before that length is set). Rejections before the listening channel is looked up: L2CAP_CR_LE_INVALID_PARAMS if cmd_len is shorter than the request or the extra bytes are not a multiple of u16, if a pending (deferred) channel with the same ident exists, if more than L2CAP_ECRED_MAX_CID SCIDs are listed, or if mtu < L2CAP_ECRED_MIN_MTU or mps < L2CAP_ECRED_MIN_MPS; L2CAP_CR_LE_BAD_PSM if psm is 0 or above L2CAP_PSM_LE_DYN_END or no listening channel exists for the psm. Once the listening channel pchan is found it is locked, and L2CAP_CR_LE_ENCRYPTION or L2CAP_CR_LE_AUTHENTICATION (depending on pchan->sec_level == BT_SECURITY_MEDIUM) is the result if smp_sufficient_security fails, L2CAP_CR_LE_UNACCEPT_PARAMS if pchan->omtu is non-zero and mtu is below it; pchan is unlocked and its reference dropped on those paths and after the SCID loop. Otherwise the result starts as L2CAP_CR_LE_SUCCESS and each SCID in order is processed: dcid[i] is set to 0; an SCID outside the dynamic LE range sets L2CAP_CR_LE_INVALID_SCID, one already in use sets L2CAP_CR_LE_SCID_IN_USE, a failed l2cap_new_connection sets L2CAP_CR_LE_NO_MEM (each overwrites the previous result, so the result is the last rejection, or success if none); an accepted SCID creates a channel, sets dcid[i] to its scid, and the response mtu/mps/credits are filled from the first created channel whose rx_credits is non-zero (the fill runs while the response credits field is still 0), and the channel is made ready or, with FLAG_DEFER_SETUP, moved to BT_CONNECT2 and its defer op called. At the end it stores the result in the response. If any channel was deferred it returns 0 without sending a response; otherwise it sends the response with l2cap_send_cmd(conn, cmd->ident, L2CAP_ECRED_CONN_RSP, ...) and returns 0.
note: Reviewer 15 right: the response fields are initialised under `if (!pdu->credits)` (l2cap_core.c:5309-5313), so a first channel with zero rx_credits does not fix them; old text said 'first accepted channel'. Reviewer 1 and 2 right (last rejection wins; no response when deferred, 5338-5339). Old text also implied the listening channel's lock is always released, but the early rejections occur before pchan is locked.

name: l2cap_recv_acldata
prose: Function l2cap_recv_acldata(hdev, handle, skb, flags) receiving an ACL data fragment; it always consumes skb. Under hci_dev_lock it looks up the hci_conn by handle; if there is none it unlocks, frees skb and returns -ENOENT. Otherwise it forces active mode, takes hcon->l2cap_data (creating it with l2cap_conn_add if absent), takes a reference with l2cap_conn_hold_unless_zero, and unlocks; if no connection could be obtained it frees skb and returns -EINVAL. With the reference held it takes conn->lock and handles flags. ACL_START, ACL_START_NO_FLUSH and ACL_COMPLETE: if a partial frame is already pending (conn->rx_skb) it logs, calls l2cap_recv_reset and l2cap_conn_unreliable(conn, ECOMM) and carries on; if skb is shorter than the length field it starts reassembly with l2cap_recv_frag using conn->mtu; if the L2CAP length matches the fragment it passes skb to l2cap_recv_frame (which takes ownership); if the fragment is longer than the frame it truncates skb to the frame length, passes it to l2cap_recv_frame and calls l2cap_conn_unreliable(conn, ECOMM); otherwise it starts reassembly with l2cap_recv_frag, and if that fails drops skb. ACL_CONT: with no pending frame it marks the connection unreliable (ECOMM) and drops skb, without l2cap_recv_reset; if the pending length header is incomplete and l2cap_recv_len fails it likewise marks it unreliable and drops, without a reset; if the fragment is longer than rx_len it calls l2cap_recv_reset, marks unreliable and drops; otherwise it appends the fragment and, when rx_len reaches 0, hands the assembled rx_skb to l2cap_recv_frame after clearing conn->rx_skb. All paths after the reference was taken unlock conn->lock, call l2cap_conn_put, and return 0. skb is either passed to l2cap_recv_frame (complete-frame start paths) or freed with kfree_skb; fragment data is copied into rx_skb on the reassembly paths, and an unrecognised flags value also frees skb.
note: Reviewer 15 right: the failed l2cap_recv_len path marks the connection unreliable and drops without l2cap_recv_reset (l2cap_core.c:7932-7935); l2cap_recv_reset is called only for an unexpected start with pending data (7869) and an over-long continuation (7945). Slice cut the head (function at 7825).

name: set_phy_configuration
prose: Static function set_phy_configuration(sk, hdev, data, len), the mgmt handler for MGMT_OP_SET_PHY_CONFIGURATION. Before taking any lock it returns mgmt_cmd_status(MGMT_STATUS_INVALID_PARAMS) if selected_phys has bits outside the supported phys or does not include every supported-but-not-configurable phy, and returns mgmt_cmd_complete(status 0) if selected_phys equals the current selection. It then takes hdev lock. Under the lock it returns mgmt_cmd_status(MGMT_STATUS_REJECTED) if the device is not powered and mgmt_cmd_status(MGMT_STATUS_BUSY) if a set-PHY-configuration command is already pending. Otherwise it recomputes pkt_type from selected_phys and stores it in hdev->pkt_type if different (this change is not undone on later failures). If the LE PHY bits are unchanged it emits mgmt_phy_configuration_changed to the other sockets when pkt_type changed, and returns mgmt_cmd_complete(status 0). If the LE PHYs changed, it allocates a pending command with mgmt_pending_new and queues set_default_phy_sync with set_default_phy_complete; if the allocation or hci_cmd_sync_queue fails, it removes the pending command (if one exists) and returns mgmt_cmd_status(MGMT_STATUS_FAILED); if queueing succeeds it returns 0 without having sent any reply (the reply is sent by the completion path). The hdev lock is released on every path on which it was taken.
note: Reviewer 15 right: after a successful hci_cmd_sync_queue the function returns 0 without sending a reply (mgmt.c:4418-4433). Old prose also omitted that hdev->pkt_type is updated before the queue step and stays updated if the queue fails (4396-4399).

name: set_bredr
prose: Static function set_bredr(sk, hdev, data, len), the mgmt handler for MGMT_OP_SET_BREDR. Without the hdev lock it returns mgmt_cmd_status with MGMT_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED if the controller is not both BR/EDR and LE capable, MGMT_STATUS_REJECTED if HCI_LE_ENABLED is not set, and MGMT_STATUS_INVALID_PARAMS if the value is neither 0 nor 1; these results are the mgmt_cmd_status return value. It then takes the hdev lock. If the value equals the current HCI_BREDR_ENABLED flag it returns send_settings_rsp. If the controller is not powered, it clears HCI_DISCOVERABLE, HCI_SSP_ENABLED, HCI_LINK_SECURITY and HCI_FAST_CONNECTABLE when disabling, toggles HCI_BREDR_ENABLED, sends the settings response and, if that succeeded, returns new_settings. If powered: disabling returns mgmt_cmd_status(MGMT_STATUS_REJECTED); enabling when BR/EDR is currently disabled returns REJECTED if a static address is set or secure connections is enabled. Otherwise it allocates a pending command and queues set_bredr_sync; if that fails (-ENOMEM or the queue error) it sends MGMT_STATUS_FAILED, frees the pending command, and returns the negative error (the status send's own result is ignored). If queueing succeeds it sets HCI_BREDR_ENABLED and returns 0 without having sent a response (the completion does that). The hdev lock is released on every path after it was taken.
note: Reviewer 15 wrong: the code does have the LE check, returning MGMT_STATUS_REJECTED when HCI_LE_ENABLED is clear (mgmt.c:6863-6865). The old prose's 'returns 0 after sending the response' is imprecise: failure of the queue returns a negative errno, and a successful queue returns 0 with the response sent later.

name: br_mdb_replace_group_star_g
prose: Static function br_mdb_replace_group_star_g(cfg, mp, pg, brmctx, flags, extack) replacing the configuration of an existing (*, G) port group. It first calls br_mdb_replace_group_srcs(cfg, pg, brmctx, extack) and returns its error immediately if it fails; in that case pg->flags, pg->filter_mode, pg->rt_protocol and pg->timer are not touched by this function. br_mdb_replace_group_srcs marks all existing sources BR_SGRP_F_DELETE, then adds or refreshes every source in cfg (a new source can fail with -ENOSPC, an already existing one with -EEXIST when NLM_F_REPLACE is not set, or with an error from the (S,G) forwarding add, in which case that source entry is deleted). If one source fails, the sources of cfg handled before it are deleted from pg (br_mdb_del_group_src, including ones that already existed) and the DELETE marks are cleared on the remaining sources; on success the sources still marked DELETE are removed. On success this function sets pg->flags = flags, pg->filter_mode and pg->rt_protocol from cfg, arms pg->timer with brmctx->multicast_membership_interval only if flags lacks MDB_PG_FLAGS_PERMANENT and cfg->filter_mode is MCAST_EXCLUDE (otherwise it deletes the timer), sends an RTM_NEWMDB notification, calls br_multicast_star_g_handle_mode(pg, cfg->filter_mode) if br_multicast_should_handle_mode(brmctx, cfg->group.proto) is true, and returns 0.
note: Both reviewers right: on failure, earlier source entries of cfg, including pre-existing ones, are deleted (br_mdb.c:937-940 via br_mdb_del_group_src) and not left intact; the old statement that a created (S,G) entry is left in the bridge could not be pointed to a line and was dropped.

name: br_multicast_port_query_expired
prose: Static function br_multicast_port_query_expired(pmctx, query), the expiry handler for a port's own query timer. It takes br->multicast_lock (pmctx->port->br) and releases it before returning. If br_multicast_port_ctx_state_stopped(pmctx) is true it does nothing more. Otherwise it gets the global bridge multicast context, increments query->startup_sent when it is below brmctx->multicast_startup_query_count, and calls br_multicast_send_query(brmctx, pmctx, query). br_multicast_send_query returns without sending or re-arming the timer if the context should not be used, multicast is disabled, the context is not a querier, no other-query state exists for the address family, or the other-query timer is pending. Otherwise it sends the query through __br_multicast_send_query and then arms query->timer (startup or normal query interval) whether or not an actual query packet was built.
note: Both reviewer claims already agree with the packet text and with br_multicast.c:1881-1918 (early returns; timer re-armed after __br_multicast_send_query regardless of its outcome). Kept; tightened.

name: br_multicast_enable
prose: Static function br_multicast_enable(query). It sets query->startup_sent = 0. Then, if timer_delete_sync_try(&query->timer) returns a value >= 0 (the timer was not pending or was deactivated, and its handler is not running) or, failing that, timer_delete(&query->timer) returns non-zero, it calls mod_timer(&query->timer, jiffies) so the timer fires immediately. If neither condition holds (for example the handler is running and the timer is not pending), the timer is left as it was and not re-armed here.
note: Both reviewers right and consistent with br_multicast.c:2105-2111 (mod_timer is conditional; startup_sent is always reset); wording tightened.

name: br_multicast_fwd_src_add
prose: Static function br_multicast_fwd_src_add(src), which installs an (S,G) forwarding entry for a group source; the caller is expected to hold the bridge multicast lock. It returns without effect if src already has BR_SGRP_F_INSTALLED, or if br_multicast_pg_to_port_ctx(src->pg) returns NULL. Otherwise it builds the (S,G) address from the group's key and the source address and calls __br_multicast_add_group with MCAST_INCLUDE, with the 'kernel' argument set to !timer_pending(&src->timer); if that returns an error pointer or NULL it returns, leaving src unchanged. On success it sets BR_SGRP_F_INSTALLED in src->flags and clears MDB_PG_FLAGS_STAR_EXCL on the new sg. If sg->rt_protocol is not RTPROT_KERNEL and MDB_PG_FLAGS_PERMANENT is set on sg (a user-added permanent entry) it returns. Otherwise it deletes sg->timer (the kernel is responsible for removal), looks up the (*,G) entry for src->pg->key.addr with br_mdb_ip_get and, if found, calls br_multicast_sg_add_exclude_ports(star_mp, sg); if not found it returns without that call.
note: Reviewers' points (timer is deleted not armed; early return for a user-added permanent sg) are right and match the packet prose (br_multicast.c:545-550); added the kernel-flag argument of __br_multicast_add_group (536-538).

name: br_process_vlan_tunnel_info
prose: Function br_process_vlan_tunnel_info(br, p, cmd, tinfo_curr, tinfo_last, changed), processing one VLAN tunnel-info attribute of a request. If tinfo_curr has BRIDGE_VLAN_INFO_RANGE_BEGIN: it returns -EINVAL if tinfo_last already has RANGE_BEGIN, otherwise copies tinfo_curr into tinfo_last and returns 0 without clearing either structure and without calling br_vlan_tunnel_info. If tinfo_curr has RANGE_END (and not RANGE_BEGIN): it returns -EINVAL if tinfo_last lacks RANGE_BEGIN, if tinfo_curr->vid < tinfo_last->vid, or if the vid difference differs from the tunid difference. Otherwise it loops v from tinfo_last->vid to tinfo_curr->vid with tunnel id starting at tinfo_last->tunid, calling br_vlan_tunnel_info(p, cmd, v, t, &curr_change); on an error it stops the loop; on success it sets *changed when this entry changed, and groups changes into notification ranges with __vlan_tunnel_handle_range (which sends RTM_NEWVLAN for completed ranges). After the loop, a pending range (v_start and v_end set) is notified with RTM_NEWVLAN even if the loop stopped on an error; then, if there was an error, it returns it without clearing tinfo_last or tinfo_curr; on full success it zeroes both and returns 0. Entries changed before an error remain changed. Otherwise (neither flag): it returns -EINVAL if tinfo_last->flags is non-zero; else it calls br_vlan_tunnel_info for tinfo_curr->vid and tunid (updating *changed there), returns its error without clearing the structures, or on success sends an RTM_NEWVLAN notification for that vid, zeroes both structures and returns 0. A NULL p is not usable for the range-end and single-VLAN cases because br_vlan_tunnel_info returns -EINVAL for a NULL port; with p NULL the RANGE_BEGIN case still just copies and returns 0.
note: Reviewer 1 and 2 right (RANGE_BEGIN does not clear; pending range notified on error, br_netlink_tunnel.c:323-327). Reviewer 15 mostly wrong: br_vlan_tunnel_info returns -EINVAL for NULL p (line 204-205), so in the range loop the first call fails and breaks before __vlan_tunnel_handle_range (which dereferences p via nbp_vlan_group) is reached; the old claim 'p may be NULL for bridge-wide operation' was still misleading and is replaced.

name: br_afspec_cmd_to_rtm
prose: Static inline function br_afspec_cmd_to_rtm(cmd). It returns RTM_NEWVLAN when cmd is RTM_SETLINK, RTM_DELVLAN when cmd is RTM_DELLINK, and 0 for any other cmd. With the values in include/uapi/linux/rtnetlink.h these are RTM_SETLINK = 19, RTM_DELLINK = 17, RTM_NEWVLAN = 112 and RTM_DELVLAN = 113. It reads no other state.
note: Reviewer 15 right: RTM_NEWVLAN is 112 and RTM_DELVLAN is 113 (rtnetlink.h:184-187; RTM_NEWLINK = 16 so DELLINK = 17, SETLINK = 19); the old prose and contract used 110/111, reviewer 1's 86/87 was also wrong.

name: br_vlan_bridge_event
prose: Function br_vlan_bridge_event(dev, event, ptr), the netdevice notifier handling for a bridge device (netdev_priv(dev) is the net_bridge); the caller holds RTNL. It starts with ret = 0, vlcmd = 0, changed = false. NETDEV_REGISTER: calls br_vlan_add(br, br->default_pvid, PVID | UNTAGGED | BRENTRY flags, &changed, NULL), stores its return value in ret, and sets vlcmd = RTM_NEWVLAN. NETDEV_UNREGISTER: sets changed = !br_vlan_delete(br, br->default_pvid) and vlcmd = RTM_DELVLAN; ret stays 0 (the delete result is not returned). NETDEV_CHANGEUPPER: reads ptr as netdev_notifier_changeupper_info and calls br_vlan_upper_change(dev, info->upper_dev, info->linking); that does nothing unless the upper device is a bridge-binding vlan device, otherwise it toggles BROPT_VLAN_BRIDGE_BINDING (set to true when linking, else to whether a bridge-binding vlan upper device still exists) and, when linking, updates that vlan device's carrier state. NETDEV_CHANGE and NETDEV_UP: if BROPT_VLAN_BRIDGE_BINDING is not set nothing happens, otherwise br_vlan_link_state_change(dev, br) walks the upper devices of dev under rcu_read_lock. Other events do nothing. After the switch, if changed is true (only possible for REGISTER with a change, or UNREGISTER when br_vlan_delete returned 0) it calls br_vlan_notify(br, NULL, br->default_pvid, 0, vlcmd). It returns ret, which is br_vlan_add's result for NETDEV_REGISTER and 0 otherwise.
note: Reviewer 1 right (UNREGISTER returns 0, br_vlan_delete result dropped, br_vlan_bridge_event line 1758) and reviewer 2 right (on unlink the option is set to whether a bind vlan remains, br_vlan_upper_change calls br_vlan_toggle_bridge_binding at br_vlan.c:1692). Both already reflected in the packet prose; tightened.

name: br_vlan_process_one_opts
prose: Static function br_vlan_process_one_opts(br, p, vg, v, tb, changed, extack) applying the VLAN options present in the attribute table tb to vlan v (RTNL held; p may be NULL for a bridge vlan). It sets *changed = false first, then handles each present attribute in this order and returns the first error, leaving earlier modifications applied (and *changed possibly already true): BRIDGE_VLANDB_ENTRY_STATE: br_vlan_modify_state returns -EINVAL for a state above BR_STATE_BLOCKING, -EBUSY with kernel STP or MST enabled; it sets *changed only if the state differs from the current one. BRIDGE_VLANDB_ENTRY_TUNNEL_INFO: br_vlan_modify_tunnel returns -EINVAL for a NULL p, for a port without BR_VLAN_TUNNEL or for an unsupported tunnel command, -ENOENT for a missing command attribute or (for RTM_SETLINK) a missing id attribute, an error from nla_parse_nested, or the result of br_vlan_tunnel_info (which sets *changed when an add succeeded or a delete returned 0; a failing delete is not reported as an error). With CONFIG_BRIDGE_IGMP_SNOOPING: BRIDGE_VLANDB_ENTRY_MCAST_ROUTER calls br_multicast_set_vlan_router, returning its error or else setting *changed = true even if the router mode was unchanged; BRIDGE_VLANDB_ENTRY_MCAST_MAX_GROUPS returns -EINVAL if p is NULL or multicast snooping is disabled on the vlan, otherwise sets the maximum and sets *changed = true even if the value is unchanged. BRIDGE_VLANDB_ENTRY_NEIGH_SUPPRESS: returns -EINVAL if p is NULL, otherwise flips BR_VLFLAG_NEIGH_SUPPRESS_ENABLED and sets *changed = true only when the requested value differs from the current flag. It returns 0 after all present attributes were processed, with extack possibly holding an error message on the failing paths.
note: Reviewer (original) right: *changed is set for mcast_max_groups and mcast_router even when the value is unchanged (br_vlan_options.c:225, 241), so it is not 'true iff something changed'; the old prose already said so. Added that a failing tunnel delete is not an error (br_netlink_tunnel.c:213-215).

name: wormhash_offset_invalid
prose: Static function wormhash_offset_invalid(off, len) checking whether an offset to a struct ebt_mac_wormhash inside match data of len bytes is invalid. It returns false if off is 0 (not present). It returns true if off is less than sizeof(struct ebt_among_info) (12 bytes) or is not a multiple of __alignof__(struct ebt_mac_wormhash) (4). Otherwise it returns whether off + sizeof(struct ebt_mac_wormhash) (1032 bytes) is greater than len. The addition is done in int, so it assumes off <= INT_MAX - 1032 (2147482615); the final comparison is against the unsigned len. It has no side effects.
contract: /*@ requires off <= 2147482615; ensures result == (off != 0 && (off < 12 || off % 4 != 0 || off + 1032 > len)); */
note: The old prose and contract used sizeof(struct ebt_among_info) = 4, which is wrong: the struct has three ints, so it is 12 bytes (ebt_among.h:49-53); sizeof(struct ebt_mac_wormhash) is 4*257+4 = 1032 (as stated). Round 1 reviewer's 12 is right; round 2 reviewer's 'it is 4' is wrong.
